purpose: The six precommitted exact-answer canaries that RQ-18 requires to be byte-identical (content) between the one-card arm A and the two-card --layer-split arm B. Definitions, scorers, expected values and prompt token files are copied verbatim from campaigns/2026/rq17-flashnext-quality/tasks.json (predeclared 2026-10-10, frozen before any RQ-17 result existed); only the generation budget is set here to RQ-18's predeclared gen 512 (greedy).
scoring: content-only (message.content); reasoning_content is retained as evidence and never scored

cells.note: sum(i*i for i in range(4)) = 0+1+4+9 = 14. The 14-vs-30 in-head arithmetic class: the fluent wrong answer 30 (summing 1..4) is the historical RL-087 defect and the precommitted stop-rule trigger
Alice>Bob>Charlie transitive chain; multi-hop logic, answer No

byte_identical_rule: For every pair, arm B's canary content bytes must equal arm A's for the same cell id, and the three pairs' arm-A contents must agree with each other. Any difference rejects (RQ-18 stop rule: 'any output difference'). The serve surface renders both arms through the same model chat template, so a byte difference is a numeric/placement difference, not a surface difference.
